slot.brief: For a first-order reaction, find the time for a stated fraction of reactant to decompose, or the fraction left after a given number of half-lives.

stem: A first-order reaction has a half-life of $20$ min. How long does it take for $\dfrac{7}{8}$ of the reactant to decompose?

verdicts.working: A remaining fraction of 1/8 equals (1/2)^3, so 3 half-lives are needed: 3 × 20 = 60 min.

working:
Fraction remaining $=1-\dfrac{7}{8}=\dfrac{1}{8}=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3$.
Thus, $3$ half-lives elapse.
$t=3(20\ \text{min})=60\ \text{min}$.

Independent check: A remaining fraction of 1/8 equals (1/2)^3, so 3 half-lives are needed: 3 × 20 = 60 min.
solution:
The fraction remaining is $1-\frac{7}{8}=\frac{1}{8}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3$, so $3$ half-lives elapse.
$$t=3(20\,\text{min})=60\,\text{min}$$
